text.text_excerpt: I absolutely had the best experience at Union Ramen. The atmosphere was so clean and vibrant. The bar was beautiful and the tiny details like records displayed paying respect to the past if this beautiful building which used to be a record store. It's things like this that makes all the difference. The food was fantastic. The chef really takes pride in ensuring each dish has been perfected before adding it to the menu. I had the opportunity to try several dishes. My favorites were the musubi, the confit oyster mushroom salad, the watermelon belly salad, the shushito peppers, the crawfish and shrimp lumpia, and last but not least the miso ramen. Wowsers. So I had a big ramen craving yesterday when I got off work. To be more specific, I had a warm broth and strong drink craving. Union Ramen seemed like the best place to fulfill my needs! I made a reservation for 6:00pm when I got off work at 5:00pm (its best to make a reservation if you plan to dine in) and soon I was transported to ramen paradise. First of all, the broth here is amazing. Its served just hot enough for you to enjoy as soon as it arrives at your table. I went with the Original Tori Ramen: Union's poultry-based broth, in-house roasted pork, bamboo shoots, scallions, seasoned egg and fried garlic and ramen noodles. If you like ramen, you've got to check out Union Ramen. Trendy, well-lit interior. Friendly service. Great food, and delicious, refreshing cocktails. Ordered the original Tori Ramen with level 3 spice on the side. Flavorful, rich broth. Perfectly cooked chewy noodles. Well-charred, tender slices of pork (very good though I've certainly had more tender). Definitely worth checking out. I will say that I was still a little hungry after eating, but may have just been the day. Otherwise, it seems that they are closed on Sunday. Finally, there is free street parking on some side streets.
